\section*{AP \({ }^{\text {® }}\) CALCULUS BC 2002 SCORING GUIDELINES}

\section*{Question 3}

The figure above shows the path traveled by a roller coaster car over the time interval \(0 \leq t \leq 18\) seconds. The position of the car at time \(t\) seconds can be modeled parametrically by \(x(t)=10 t+4 \sin t, y(t)=(20-t)(1-\cos t)\),
![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/df9396ad-9aa0-4020-9582-0dfd4c261f19-1.jpg?height=200&width=801&top_left_y=314&top_left_x=1160)
where \(x\) and \(y\) are measured in meters. The derivatives of these functions are given by \(x^{\prime}(t)=10+4 \cos t, y^{\prime}(t)=(20-t) \sin t+\cos t-1\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Find the slope of the path at time \(t=2\). Show the computations that lead to your answer.
\item[(b)] Find the acceleration vector of the car at the time when the car's horizontal position is \(x=140\).
\item[(c)] Find the time \(t\) at which the car is at its maximum height, and find the speed, in \(\mathrm{m} / \mathrm{sec}\), of the car at this time.
\item[(d)] For \(0<t<18\), there are two times at which the car is at ground level \((y=0)\). Find these two times and write an expression that gives the average speed, in \(\mathrm{m} / \mathrm{sec}\), of the car between these two times. Do not evaluate the expression.
\item[(a)]
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text { Slope } & =\left.\frac{d y}{d x}\right|_{t=2}=\frac{y^{\prime}(2)}{x^{\prime}(2)}=\frac{18 \sin 2+\cos 2-1}{10+4 \cos 2} \\
& =1.793 \text { or } 1.794
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(b)]
\[
\begin{aligned}
& x(t)=10 t+4 \sin t=140 ; t_{0}=13.647083 \\
& x^{\prime \prime}\left(t_{0}\right)=-3.529, y^{\prime \prime}\left(t_{0}\right)=1.225 \text { or } 1.226 \\
& \text { Acceleration vector is }<-3.529,1.225> \\
& \text { or }<-3.529,1.226>
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(c)]
\[
\begin{aligned}
& y^{\prime}(t)=(20-t) \sin t+\cos t-1=0 \\
& t_{1}=3.023 \text { or } 3.024 \text { at maximum height } \\
& \begin{aligned}
\text { Speed } & =\sqrt{\left(x^{\prime}\left(t_{1}\right)\right)^{2}+\left(y^{\prime}\left(t_{1}\right)\right)^{2}}=\left|x^{\prime}\left(t_{1}\right)\right| \\
& =6.027 \text { or } 6.028
\end{aligned}
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(d)]
\[
\begin{aligned}
& y(t)=0 \text { when } t=2 \pi \text { and } t=4 \pi \\
& \text { Average speed }=\frac{1}{2 \pi} \int_{2 \pi}^{4 \pi} \sqrt{\left(x^{\prime}(t)\right)^{2}+\left(y^{\prime}(t)\right)^{2}} d t \\
& =\frac{1}{2 \pi} \int_{2 \pi}^{4 \pi} \sqrt{(10+4 \cos t)^{2}+((20-t) \sin t+\cos t-1)^{2}} d t
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{itemize}
\[
1 \text { : answer using } \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{d y}{d t} / \frac{d x}{d t}
\]
\[
2\left\{\begin{aligned}
1: & \text { identifies acceleration vector } \\
& \text { as derivative of velocity vector } \\
1: & \text { computes acceleration vector } \\
& \text { when } x=140
\end{aligned}\right.
\]
\[
3 \begin{cases}1: & \text { sets } y^{\prime}(t)=0 \\ 1: & \text { selects first } t>0 \\ 1: & \text { speed }\end{cases}
\]
\[
3\left\{\begin{array}{l}
1: t=2 \pi, t=4 \pi \\
1: \text { limits and constant } \\
1: \text { integrand }
\end{array}\right.
\]
